keyFindings.text: **`research.md` still carries the 486-word `--depth-mode` table cell that the review already collapsed in `review.md`.** The research cell restates seeding, all six admission checks, the cap arithmetic, the 50/35/15 split, the derived-budget formula, the fan-out floors and the stop-veto list in one row, while the review surface now says four lines and links to its protocol. That is the same discoverability defect the fan-out review found in `review.md` (OPUS-F004-P2-004), fixed only on one side. One concrete change: replace `.skilled/commands/deep/research.md:107` with the `review.md` pointer shape and move the long form to `.skilled/commands/deep/assets/deep-research-presentation.txt` under one "Expansive depth" heading. Value: an operator scanning flags sees the flag, not the design. Effort S. Risk low (docs only). [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/deep/research.md:107] [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/deep/review.md:100] [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/deep/assets/deep-research-presentation.txt:74]

**Question intake has two paths, and this lineage's own dashboard shows the duplicate state it produces.** Init wrote six questions into strategy Section 3; the fan-out root had already written three frontier rows to `inbox.jsonl`; the reducer imported both sets as `legacy-import` and `frontier`, so the dashboard reports 9 open questions that are really 6 topics with 3 near-duplicates. The strategy template still tells the operator that direct Section 3 edits work as a compatibility path (`.skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/deep-research/assets/deep-research-strategy.md:61-68`). One concrete change: have `step_create_strategy` write key questions to `inbox.jsonl` with `origin: "analyst-strategy"` and leave Section 3 empty; the reducer then owns the only intake. Value: one question list, no `question_conflict` noise, honest 6/6 progress. Effort M. Risk medium (older packets depend on legacy import; keep the import read-only for them). [SOURCE: specs/system-deep-loop/loop-architecture/002-graph-engineering/007-expansive-depth-mode/research/lineages/deepseek/deep-research-dashboard.md:34] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/deep-research/assets/deep-research-strategy.md:61] [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/deep/assets/deep-research.yaml:928]

**The budget warning never reaches a fan-out operator.** `seedBudget` is the only place that says "no growth slot past depth 1" (`.skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/runtime/scripts/frontier-admit.cjs:521`), and its CLI entry is skipped on a lineage (`deep-research.yaml:839`); the fan-out root's `step_frontier_seed` prints admitted/pruned nodes but no per-lineage budget, and `fanout-run.cjs` knows the partition and every lineage's `iterations` value at spawn time. One concrete change: have `fanout-run.cjs` print, per lineage, `<label>: <iterations> iterations, <growth slots> growth slots past depth 1`, and raise the same warning when the count is zero. Value: budget sizing becomes visible where the money is spent. Effort S. Risk low. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/runtime/scripts/frontier-admit.cjs:521] [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/deep/assets/deep-research.yaml:839] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/runtime/scripts/fanout-run.cjs:4007]

**The fan-out dry-run prints `frontier_scope: []` for an unseeded expansive run, which is indistinguishable from "this lineage was dealt no nodes".** The preview path builds `frontier_scope` from `resolveFrontierPartition` over the on-disk store, and on a first run the store does not exist yet because seeding happens after the preview; the docs explain the empty value in prose instead of encoding it. One concrete change: emit `frontier_scope: null` plus `frontier_scope_status: "pending-seed"` when `depthMode === 'expansive'` and no store exists, and print a one-line runner warning that scopes appear only after the seed. Value: removes a false-negative read of the most important preview field. Effort S. Risk low. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/runtime/scripts/fanout-run.cjs:4007] [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/deep/research.md:145] [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/deep/assets/deep-research-presentation.txt:31]

**There is no first-class way to rerun one failed lineage; recovery today is hand-editing the fan-out config.** `fanout-run.cjs` exposes no `--lineage`/`--only`/`--retry-failed` filter, and `readStoredLineageSessionId` deliberately returns `null` when a lineage config is `complete`, so a second invocation mints a fresh `fanout-<label>-<runId>` session for *every* lineage in the matrix and re-enters the same directory. A completed lineage then trips the `on_completed_session` halt, writes no new iteration, and fails `checkLineageCompletion` on the stale terminal row. The committed packet shows the workaround: `review/fanout-config-recovery.json` is a hand-rewritten one-executor matrix that re-runs only `deepseek`. One concrete change: add a repeatable `--only-lineage=LABEL` to `fanout-run.cjs`, filter `allLineages` before the frontier partition, and report filtered-out lineages as `skipped_complete` in the summary. Value: turns a config edit plus full re-spend into one flag. Effort M. Risk medium (partition and summary arithmetic must exclude skipped lineages). [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/runtime/scripts/fanout-run.cjs:772] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/runtime/scripts/fanout-run.cjs:3935] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/runtime/scripts/fanout-run.cjs:4837] [SOURCE: specs/system-deep-loop/loop-architecture/002-graph-engineering/007-expansive-depth-mode/review/fanout-config-recovery.json:1]

**`reasoningEffort` is a per-kind lottery in an otherwise shared matrix.** The Zod schema accepts it for every kind (`executor-config.ts:91`), but the supported-field table rejects it for `cli-cursor`, `cli-devin` and `cli-mistral-vibe` because those ids bake the tier into the model name (`:117-141`), so one `--executors` matrix that sets effort for all lineages fails on the three that cannot honor it. One concrete change: keep the field accepted for every kind, map it in the adapter (`--effort`, `--variant`, `--thinking`, or a `#effort` model suffix), and report `effortApplied: "flag" | "baked" | "none"` in `effectiveConfig`, with a loud warning when a requested tier cannot be honored. Value: one matrix works across all eight kinds. Effort M. Risk medium (a silent downgrade would be worse than the current hard failure; the warning is the contract). [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/runtime/lib/deep-loop/executor-config.ts:91] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/runtime/lib/deep-loop/executor-config.ts:117] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/runtime/scripts/fanout-run.cjs:2659]

**Failure classification keeps kind-specific branches in the shared worker instead of in the adapter table.** `fanout-run.cjs:4695` ignores a non-zero exit for `cli-pi` only, `:4664-4667` runs extra completion validators for `cli-deepseek-harness` and `cli-mistral-vibe`, and `:4714` maps quota exhaustion to its own reason across all kinds. The worker therefore knows four kinds by name, and a new kind must edit it. One concrete change: let each entry in `LINEAGE_COMMAND_ADAPTERS` (`:3557-3567`) carry `exitPolicy` and `completionValidator`, and have the worker classify from those fields only. Value: one failure model; new kinds add data, not branches. Effort M. Risk medium (the pi tolerance and the vibe partial verdict must move without behavior change). [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/runtime/scripts/fanout-run.cjs:3557] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/runtime/scripts/fanout-run.cjs:4695] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/runtime/scripts/fanout-run.cjs:4664]

**Log shape and resume are already at parity; the remaining asymmetry is `native`.** Every kind writes the same `logs/fanout-lineage.out` and `.err` with rotation (`fanout-run.cjs:4640-4645`), and every kind resumes through `readStoredLineageSessionId` (`:772`), so those two axes need no contract. But `native` is listed in `EXECUTOR_KINDS` and in `LINEAGE_COMMAND_ADAPTERS`, yet `buildNativeLineageCommand` throws on OpenCode v2 by construction (`:2640-2645`), so a matrix that names `native` works or fails on the host's OpenCode major version. One concrete change: remove `native` from the fan-out adapter table and reject it in `preflightFanoutCapabilities` with the same message, or gate it behind an explicit `native-command-surface` kind. Value: removes a version-dependent trap from the matrix. Effort S. Risk low. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/runtime/scripts/fanout-run.cjs:4640] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/runtime/scripts/fanout-run.cjs:2640] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/runtime/lib/deep-loop/executor-config.ts:11]

**The "single executor contract" already exists as data — but only half of it is printed.** `EXECUTOR_KIND_FLAG_SUPPORT` (`executor-config.ts:112-142`) declares which config fields each kind accepts, and `EXECUTOR_PREVENTIVE_SANDBOX_CAPABILITY` (`:159-169`) declares whether the kind's sandbox is a real OS boundary, a compensating control, or nothing. `finalizeLineageCommand` then emits `sandboxMode` and `permissionMode` in `effectiveConfig` (`fanout-run.cjs:2507-2516`) and the preview prints exactly those two, so a `cli-pi` or `cli-devin` lineage shows `sandboxMode: workspace-write` even though the matrix says `false` (no preventive boundary). One concrete change: add `sandboxEnforcement: "preventive" | "compensating" | "none"` to `effectiveConfig` from the capability matrix and print it beside `sandbox` in the preview and `invocation-metadata.json`. Value: ends the "which CLI actually confines" question with one field. Effort S. Risk low. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/runtime/lib/deep-loop/executor-config.ts:159] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/runtime/scripts/fanout-run.cjs:2507]

**The six per-kind single-executor branches in each YAML are the same command with a different `--executor` argument.** `deep-research.yaml:1762-1837` has eight `if_cli_*` branches; six of them (claude-code, cursor, devin, pi, opencode, codex) run `dispatch-iteration.cjs --executor <kind>` with identical arguments, and only `cli-deepseek-harness` (extra `--spec-folder`) and `cli-mistral-vibe` (fail closed) differ. `deep-review.yaml` carries the same duplication. One concrete change: collapse the six into one `if_cli` branch whose `--executor` is `{config.executor.kind}`, keep the two special branches, in both YAMLs. Value: roughly 60 lines removed per YAML and one place to add the next kind. Effort S. Risk low (`dispatch-iteration.cjs` already accepts the kind as a value). [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/deep/assets/deep-research.yaml:1762] [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/deep/assets/deep-research.yaml:1812] [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/deep/assets/deep-research.yaml:1738] [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/deep/assets/deep-research.yaml:1752]

**No host-measured duration reaches the iteration record, so every latency claim rests on model-written timestamps that mix queue, model and idle time.** The fan-out runner already computes `slotDurationMs` and the dispatch receipt carries it (`fanout-run.cjs:4058`), but the iteration row has no `durationMs`; this lineage's own rows have none, and the archive spans (10 iterations in 31 min, 3 in 36 min) cannot be separated into model time and queue time. One concrete change: stamp the host-measured `durationMs` (and `slotDurationMs` when present) onto the iteration row before the gateway append, or require it in the prompt pack's OUTPUT CONTRACT. Value: makes the cost question answerable per iteration instead of per run. Effort S. Risk low. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/runtime/scripts/fanout-run.cjs:4058] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/deep-research/assets/prompt-pack-iteration.md.tmpl:67] [SOURCE: specs/system-deep-loop/loop-architecture/002-graph-engineering/007-expansive-depth-mode/review-archive/20261119T183614Z/deep-review-state.jsonl:1]

**Per-iteration cost is dominated by cache re-read of the same context, not by output.** The live playbooks measure 0.33M input, 0.03M output and 6.2M cache-read tokens for one added iteration, and 0.57M-0.75M input with 11.9M-13.7M cache-read over three iterations; at 24 iterations that is roughly 8M input and 150M cache-read. The prompt pack restates the full research topic and the whole state summary every iteration (`prompt-pack-iteration.md.tmpl:12-19`), which is exactly the re-read. One concrete change: render the topic as a path plus a one-line digest in the per-iteration pack (the leaf already reads `deep-research-config.json`), and keep only the delta summary for the last three iterations. Value: the cheapest cut in the whole budget, because it removes repeated input on every iteration. Effort S. Risk low (the leaf reads the config anyway). [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/deep-research/manual-testing-playbook/entry-points-and-modes/live-extend-expansive-research-run.md:34] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/deep-research/manual-testing-playbook/entry-points-and-modes/live-expansive-research-two-node-frontier.md:34] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/deep-research/assets/prompt-pack-iteration.md.tmpl:12]

**Setup costs 3-10 minutes per lineage before iteration 1, and a fan-out pays it once per lineage.** Measured from config `createdAt` to the first iteration timestamp: opus 3 min, deepseek 4 min, the 10-iteration archive run 10 min, the 3-iteration archive run 6 min. The root has already resolved the topic, seeded the frontier and partitioned it before spawning, so most of that work is repeated inside each child. One concrete change: when `fanout_lineage_artifact_dir` is bound, skip the context-ladder ripgrep and the resource-map scan in the child and read the root's prepared `prior_context`/seed files instead; keep the config, strategy and registry creation because those are lineage-owned. Value: 3-9 minutes saved per lineage on a 3-lineage fan-out. Effort M. Risk medium (a lineage that starts without its own context summary must still render a valid prompt). [SOURCE: specs/system-deep-loop/loop-architecture/002-graph-engineering/007-expansive-depth-mode/review/lineages/opus/deep-review-config.json:1] [SOURCE: specs/system-deep-loop/loop-architecture/002-graph-engineering/007-expansive-depth-mode/review-archive/20261119T153733Z/deep-review-state.jsonl:1] [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/deep/assets/deep-research.yaml:117]

**The 24-iteration ceiling is unreachable at the measured 8-11 minutes per iteration under the default 120-minute duration budget; the duration stop binds first.** The review protocol already admits it ("At about seven to eight minutes an iteration, a 24-iteration review can reach `maxDurationMinutes` (120) before its iteration cap"), and one committed archive run shows the operator's workaround: `review-archive/20261119T153733Z` raised `maxDurationMinutes` to 360 for 10 iterations. At 8-11 min/iteration, 120 minutes funds 11-15 iterations, not 24, so the advertised cap is not the effective one. One concrete change: at config creation, derive the default duration budget from the iteration cap (`max(120, 10 × maxIterations)` for review, `max(120, 12 × maxIterations)` for research) or print a one-line warning that names the iteration at which the duration stop will bind. Value: the cap an operator reads is the cap the run can reach. Effort S. Risk low (an explicit `--max-duration`/config value still wins). [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/deep-review/references/protocol/loop-protocol.md:464] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/deep-research/manual-testing-playbook/entry-points-and-modes/live-expansive-research-two-node-frontier.md:34] [SOURCE: specs/system-deep-loop/loop-architecture/002-graph-engineering/007-expansive-depth-mode/review-archive/20261119T153733Z/deep-review-config.json:1]

**The 50/35/15 split starves the depth-1 band on a review: with three nodes per lineage and four dimensions each, depth 1 needs 12 of 24 iterations, exactly its 50% share, leaving no room for growth.** `applyBandBudget` closes every open node in a band once `spent >= cap × share` (`frontier-admit.cjs:360-395`), and the review protocol tells the operator to set `--max-iterations` to at least `2 × ceil(nodes/lineages) × dimensions` — i.e. to double the budget so the fixed 50% happens to cover depth 1. One concrete change: size `budgetSplit.depth1` from the seed (`nodesPerLineage × dimensions / maxIterations`, capped at 0.7) and give the remainder to depth 2 and 3, instead of a fixed 0.5. Value: a wide review funds its seeds before it funds growth, without operator arithmetic. Effort M. Risk medium-high (it changes when budget closes fire; the existing split must remain the default for default-mode runs). [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/runtime/scripts/frontier-admit.cjs:360] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/deep-review/references/protocol/loop-protocol.md:464]

**Every `observability-events.jsonl` row carries `subject.run_id: null`, so the event stream cannot be joined to a run or a lineage.** The payload names the label but not the run, and `run_id` is a first-class field on the envelope that is simply left empty. One concrete change: set `subject.run_id` (and `subject.label`) on every emitted event. Value: partial-run forensics and any external dashboard can correlate without parsing free text. Effort S. Risk low. [SOURCE: specs/system-deep-loop/loop-architecture/002-graph-engineering/007-expansive-depth-mode/review/observability-events.jsonl:1] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/runtime/scripts/fanout-run.cjs:4801]

**The dashboard shows band spend but not per-node visits or status, so three single-node passes and three passes on one node look identical.** This lineage's dashboard after three iterations reports `Frontier size: 3 nodes (3 open…)`, `Revisits: 0` and `Budget depth1: 3 of 5 iterations spent`; nothing says each node was visited exactly once, and the registry already holds the data (`frontierNodeVisitRecords` in `reduce-state.cjs:2491`). One concrete change: add a per-node table to the dashboard frontier section (`nodeId, depth, visits, status, band, lastIteration`). Value: an operator can see a starved or a monopolised node before the band closes it. Effort S. Risk low. [SOURCE: specs/system-deep-loop/loop-architecture/002-graph-engineering/007-expansive-depth-mode/research/lineages/deepseek/deep-research-dashboard.md:108] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/deep-research/scripts/reduce-state.cjs:2491]

**The partial-run summary reports only aggregate failure classes, never which lineage failed or how to rerun it.** `orchestration-summary.json` carries `total/succeeded/failed/all_failed`, a `failure_classes` count map and `timestamp_anomalies`; it has no per-lineage `{label, status, reason, rerun_command}` array. An operator whose deepseek lineage died on a 429 sees `failed: 1` and `quota: 1`, then has to open `orchestration-status.log` and the lineage logs to learn which one and what to run next. One concrete change: add a `lineages: [{label, status, reason, failure_class, rerun_command}]` array to the summary, with `rerun_command` the original argv narrowed to that label (`--only-lineage` from the iteration-1 finding, or the documented current workaround). Value: one file answers "what failed and what do I type". Effort S. Risk low. [SOURCE: specs/system-deep-loop/loop-architecture/002-graph-engineering/007-expansive-depth-mode/review/orchestration-summary.json:1] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/runtime/scripts/fanout-run.cjs:4714] [SOURCE: specs/system-deep-loop/loop-architecture/002-graph-engineering/007-expansive-depth-mode/review/fanout-config-recovery.json:1]

**The quota failure is detected but not turned into an instruction.** `fanout-run.cjs:4714-4717` produces `lineage <label> ...: provider quota exhausted (<cause>)`, while the single-executor workflow already carries the actionable sentence "Switch executor or wait, then resume this run" (`deep-research.yaml:1898`). The fan-out summary and the error line do not carry that clause or any resume step. One concrete change: append the same recovery clause plus the lineage-specific resume step to the quota failure message and to the summary's `rerun_command`. Value: the failure names the action, not just the cause. Effort S. Risk low. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/runtime/scripts/fanout-run.cjs:4714] [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/deep/assets/deep-research.yaml:1898]

**This lineage is a live instance of the budget split under-funding its nodes: 10 iterations give the depth-1 band 5 visits for 3 nodes, but each node needs a first pass and a verification pass.** The dashboard itself reports `Budget depth1: 3 of 5 iterations spent` after three single-node passes, which leaves two visits for the remaining second passes on all three nodes. The fan-out floor for a CLI lineage is 10 (`research.md:107`), independent of how many nodes it is dealt, so a 3-node share is funded as if it were a 1-node share. One concrete change: raise the CLI lineage floor to `max(10, 2 × dealtNodes + 2)` (research) so every dealt node is funded for a first and a verification pass. Value: removes the starvation this run has to work around by closing nodes early. Effort S. Risk low (the cap is still bounded by the explicit `iterations` value). [SOURCE: specs/system-deep-loop/loop-architecture/002-graph-engineering/007-expansive-depth-mode/research/lineages/deepseek/deep-research-dashboard.md:113] [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/deep/research.md:107] [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/deep/assets/deep-research.yaml:844]

**`runLineageBuiltin` forces `workspace-write` for cursor, devin and pi, so a configured `read-only` request is silently upgraded to a writable run.** `dispatch-iteration.cjs:459-468` sets `const sandboxMode = 'workspace-write'` and passes it to `buildLineageCommand` for all three kinds, discarding `context.sandboxMode`. The fan-out path resolves the requested sandbox and fails closed when a kind cannot honor it (`fanout-run.cjs:3963-3966`, `:2501-2506`). One concrete change: pass the configured sandbox and let `buildLineageCommand` refuse an unhonorable request, as it already does for `cli-opencode`. Value: growth follows value, not arrival order. Effort M. Risk medium (a model-authored priority must not be trusted over the caps). [SOURCE: https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.10601]

ruledOutDirections.text: Reading the presentation assets as an independent intake surface: they restate the same long-form budget prose as `research.md`, so collapsing `research.md:107` to a pointer does not remove the last copy, it moves the copy to the asset that already owns setup detail.

Searching for a literal "8-11 minute setup" string: the only match is a retired tool-call budget in a changelog; the setup-time reading has no textual anchor. The cost node must measure per-iteration wall clock instead.

Treating `--frontier-max-depth`/`--frontier-max-nodes` refusal as an undocumented trap: both command docs and both presentation assets state the fan-out refusal at the flag row, so the surface is documented even though the refusal is only visible by running a dry run.
Proposing a new config schema: `executor-config.ts` is already the single schema; the gap is that two derived facts (enforcement class, effort application) are not carried into the output.
Searching for per-kind resume flags: resume is config-driven for every kind through `readStoredLineageSessionId`, so there is nothing to unify.
Treating log shape as a parity gap: all kinds already write the same rotated `fanout-lineage.out/.err` pair, so no change is needed there.
Blaming fan-out concurrency for the 429: the review run used concurrency 2 and the quota failure hit one lineage; the recovery gap is the real defect, and iteration 1 already records it.
Searching for a measured setup time in the playbooks: the only figure recorded is per-iteration cost, so setup had to be measured from the committed `createdAt` and first-iteration timestamps.

Treating model price as the main lever: the measured cost is dominated by cache-read of unchanged context and by wall-clock latency, not by output tokens, so a cheaper model changes the multiplier, not the shape.
Claiming the dashboard hides band spend: it prints all three bands and their allotments; the missing dimension is per-node detail, not the band budget.
Proposing a new summary file: `orchestration-summary.json` is already the operator's terminal artifact; it only needs the per-lineage array.

Searching for a documented fan-out resume procedure in `research.md`: the command doc covers `--lineage-mode=resume` and `--extend` for a single run, but has no fan-out recovery section; the only evidence of the real procedure is the committed recovery config.
Claiming the six YAML branches need different arguments: only claude (config dir) and dsh (spec folder) add a flag, and both are already optional in the shared script.
Looking for a review-specific claude builder in the fan-out path: there is one builder for both loops, which is exactly why the single-executor branch diverged unnoticed.
Treating the forced `workspace-write` as a bug in the builder: the builder honors what it is given; the silent narrowing happens in the caller.
Looking for an `on_failure` branch in `step_fanout_spawn`: there is none, so the parent has no partial path to take.
Requiring a new recovery command: the runner already holds every input a rerun needs, so the fix is serialization, not a new workflow.
Treating exit 2 as a deliberate safety stop: it protects the merge from partial input but gives the operator no merge at all, which is the opposite of the failure's cost.
Adding a new registry file: the projection is the right carrier; it already has the visit function.
Claiming both dashboards hide band spend: both print the three bands and their allotments; the missing piece is per-node detail and the active-node line.
Searching for a review-side per-node table in the committed review dashboard: it reports the same aggregate size and revisits, so the per-node table is absent on both sides, not only in research.

Collapsing the two reducers into one file: the review reducer carries dimension coverage and the research reducer carries novelty questions; the shared part is the frontier projection, not the whole reducer.
Deleting `frontier-admit.cjs` as a whole: it is shared by both reducers and both loops, so it is the one place the frontier rules already live; the duplication is around it, not inside it.
Looking for a shared YAML macro system: the workflow format has no include mechanism, so duplication must be collapsed at the step level, not by templating.
Searching for dead `if_cli_*` branches: all eight are reachable, so the deletion is a merge, not a dead-code removal.
Admitting pivot candidates with a full reworked transaction: the three D-011-10 blockers each have a one-line answer; a transaction rewrite is not needed.
Looking for a research `activeNodeId` in the registry: the research projection does not emit one, which is why the node-scoped counter cannot be enabled by a flag alone.
Weakening the live completion check to fix the audit: a live attempt that writes nothing must still fail, so the fallback has to be scoped to a completed historical config.
Adopting a full MCTS search (LATS-style) for the frontier: the measured runs are 10-24 iterations, too shallow for tree search to pay for its branching overhead; a priority field is the cheap 80%.

Copying Anthropic's synchronous lead-agent loop: this runtime already has the fan-out pool and per-lineage state, so the transferable part is the effort-scaling table and the checkpoint/resume discipline, not the topology.

Looking for a published stuck-detection rule in these systems: Anthropic handles failure with retries and checkpoints, LangChain with iteration caps, ToT with evaluation; none publishes a per-node stuck counter, so this runtime's per-node counter is ahead of the public prior art and should be kept.
